Appendix — how these were found

Re-run 2026-10-15 21:30 UTC. Step 1: 40 single flags with >=3 keys spiking. Dropped as artifacts (baseline ~0, TT edited Oct 14): g-ip-asn-reputation-high-risk-with-session-signal, g-ip-connection-type-velocity-short-term-abuse-cloud-asn, g-atm-all-agents, plus the g-ip-datacenter / hosting / shared-egress family already excluded on Oct 14. g--e-g-ja4-suspicious-verification-patterns is Ensemble (re-dated daily), kept. Step 2 over 16 flags found one new attack combination, now tracked: di-short-count-300-fp-pixel-ratio-1 + g-device-parameter-spoofing + ja4-dict-1-challenger. Separately, g-ip-residential-proxy-user-ip jumped ~3.5x on Oct 14 across ~50 keys at once (sampled 10k/day -> 35-38k/day) with no TT edit since Aug 3. A same-day step across that many keys looks like an IP-intel feed or list change rather than one attack. Check with the IP-intel owners before building on it; not tracked.
